title: Retrocore project
description: A Retrocore project (retrocore.json): the CPU its code keeps to, its sources and defines, and the machine × environment targets it builds for. At a repository's root it can instead list the folders of the repository's projects.

why.description: What the machine keeps there, for a reserved area.

step.description: A host-side tool run before assembly, started in the project's folder. Paths are relative to the project's folder, and ${obj} in an input, an output or an argument is its intermediate folder, obj/.

tool.description: A C# file-based app (.cs), run as dotnet run <file> -- <args>, or a project (.csproj), run as dotnet run --project <file> -- <args>.

args.description: The tool's arguments. ${obj} is the intermediate folder; an argument that is exactly ${in} or ${out} stands for every input or output. Without args the tool gets the inputs, then the outputs.

in.description: The files the tool reads; a change to one runs the step again.

out.description: The files the tool writes, such as ${obj}/game.bin for an .incbin.

root.description: A repository's root file that lists its projects.

projects.description: The folders of the repository's projects, each with its own retrocore.json.

sdk.description: The SDK's major version the project is written against.

name.description: The project's name, which names its output files: letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.'. Defaults to its folder's name.

cpu.description: The CPU the code keeps to. A target can raise it (r65c02 on an enhanced IIe), never lower it.

sources.description: The files every target assembles, in order: paths or patterns (* and ? in a name, ** for any folders), relative to the project's folder. Each target assembles src/platform/<family>/'s .s and .asm files first, then src/platform/<model>/'s, then src/platform/<environment>/'s, a later folder's file taking the place of an earlier one's at the same path within its folder, and these after them.

steps.description: Host-side build steps that run, in order, before any target assembles. A step whose tool and inputs are unchanged since it last ran, and whose outputs are as it left them, is skipped.

defines.description: Symbols every target defines before its sources.

entry.description: The entry point's label; defaults to the first byte the project's own sources emit, after the platform folders' code, or to the first section when they emit none.

output.description: The folder build output goes in, each target's in a folder of its name; intermediate files go in obj/<target>/.

targets.description: The project's targets by name. The name also names the target's output folders.

machine.description: The machine, as Retrocore: Start Machine and favorites name it.

environment.description: How the program is loaded and started, and which system calls it may make. Every machine runs bare; each other environment runs on the machines the SDK plan pairs it with. bare, wozmon, dos33, dfs, basic, sos, prodos and level2 build yet.

cpu.description: Raises the project's CPU for this target; the machine must run it.

options.description: The machine's launch options, such as ramKilobytes, as a launch configuration gives them. They cannot give what the project and its targets decide: type, request, name, project, target, machine, model, rom, source, program, basic, debugFile, dialect, linkerConfiguration, machineState, dos, loadAddress, entryAddress, executable or basicSource; stopOnEntry and checkContracts stay the launch's.

cards.description: The cards in the machine's slots, by slot, such as { "4": "mockingboard" }, as a saved machine lists them.

defines.description: Symbols this target defines, over the project's.

sources.description: Sources added for this target only, after the platform folders' and the project's.

linkerConfiguration.description: An ld65-style linker configuration, relative to the project's folder.

memoryMap.description: Changes to the SDK's memory map for the target's machine, environment and RAM (Sdk/1/environments/<environment>/<name>.map.json, the name being the first the SDK has of <catalog id>-<RAM>k, <catalog id>, <family>-<RAM>k and <family>), which the build makes its linker configuration from when the target gives none, and checks every section against.

load.description: Where the program loads, in free RAM, instead of the map's.

free.description: Areas to use as free RAM, taken out of the reserved areas they overlap, such as hi-res page 1 for a game that draws there.

reserved.description: Areas the program must leave alone, taken out of free RAM, each with the reason.

zeroPage.description: The zero-page bytes the program may use, instead of the map's: each a byte or a run, such as "$06-$09".

files.description: Data files put beside the program on its disk, such as a step's output: each a path relative to the project's folder (which may give ${obj}), or an object with its path, its name on the disk and the load address the disk records. An environment with no disk takes none.

path.description: The file, relative to the project's folder; ${obj} is its obj/ folder.

name.description: Its name on the disk, instead of one made from its file name.

address.description: The load address the disk records for it, where the disk records one.

image.description: Whether the target builds its environment's disk or tape image (true, the default), or not (false), or an object whose template names the disk the image starts from or whose boot names the image a launch boots. An environment that builds no image takes none.

template.description: The disk the image starts from, relative to the project's folder; ${obj} is its obj/ folder.

boot.description: Which of its environment's images a launch boots, where it builds more than one: basic's tape (the default) or disk.

bootImage.description: The folder of the boot media or device dumps the environment needs where they are not SDK sources, relative to the project's folder (${obj} is its obj/ folder), such as the 4040's ROMs a basic target's disk boots with, or ProDOS 2.4.3's disk a prodos target's disk is built from. They are found there by their hashes, then where the environment looks: for a basic target, the launch's romDirectory and the c4040 folder beside it, RETROCORE_PET_ROMS and RETROCORE_CACHE; for a prodos target, RETROCORE_CACHE. An environment that boots from the SDK's sources alone takes none.

dialect.description: The files' dialect; defaults to native unless a file's first-line pragma names one.

kind.description: The files' language: asm, or basic, which loads but does not build yet.

enumDescriptions: The NMOS 6502.
The instructions every 65C02 has (the 65SC02's).
The Rockwell R65C02, with the bit instructions, as the enhanced IIe runs it.
The WDC W65C02S, with WAI and STP as well.
The Intel 8080.
The Intel 8085.
The Zilog Z80, which also runs 8080 code.
The Motorola 6809.
A raw binary loaded straight into RAM, with the ROM's routines only. All machines.
Woz Monitor hex to type in, and an ACI tape (WAV). The Apple-1.
A B file on a DOS 3.3 disk that its HELLO starts. The Apple II, II Plus and IIe.
A SYS file at $2000 on a disk with ProDOS 2.4.3, found by its hash, which starts it. The II Plus with 64K, and the IIe.
A SOS.INTERP at $2000 on a SOS 1.3 boot disk built from the SDK's sources. The Apple III.
A PRG with a BASIC SYS line, on a TAP tape and a 4040 disk. The PET.
A *RUN file on a DFS disk that its !BOOT runs, and a UEF tape. The BBC Micro.
A .COM file under CP/M. The Apple II and IIe with a SoftCard, the TRS-80 Model 4, the Altair and the Kaypro II. Not yet supported.
A Level II SYSTEM tape (CAS) that the ROM's SYSTEM command loads and / starts. The TRS-80 Model I and III.
A /CMD load module. The TRS-80 Model I, III and 4. Not yet supported.
A DECB .BIN under Color BASIC. The Color Computer. Not yet supported.
A DECB .BIN under Disk BASIC. The Color Computer. Not yet supported.
